name: Han Tao
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2016-2017); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Han Tao chairs Goldenmax International Group, a supplier of laminate products used to make printed circuit boards.
Han worked at a watch parts factory in Hangzhou from 1977-83, attended university and later worked for the company that became Goldenmax.
Goldenmax International Group listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Lim Hariyanto Wijaya Sarwono
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); Wikidata (2019)
forbes_bio: Lim and his family own a majority stake in Singapore-listed palm oil producer Bumitama Agri; its plantations are located in Indonesia.
His son Lim Gunawan Hariyanto is CEO of the family's Harita Group.
Harita Group also owns the majority of listed bauxite mining firm Cita Mineral Investindo. Lim's integrated nickel processing company Trimegah Bangun Persada raised $650 million in a 2023 IPO.
Lim's father emigrated from China to East Kalimantan and reportedly opened a grocery store in 1915.
His daughter Christina is executive director of Bumitama Agri.
forbes_facts: The family group's name Harita comes from Lim Hariyanto and wife Rita.
Lim started pursuing higher education in his late 60s, and obtained a doctoral degree in business administration from Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2005 at age 77.

name: Yuji Otsuka
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Yuji Otsuka is the son of the late Minoru Otsuka, who founded Otsuka Corp. in 1961, a software developer and supplier of office copy machines.
Yuji, a former banker, took over as CEO when Minoru retired in 2001.
Otsuka's forecasted revenue for 2024 is $6.6 billion.

name: Alan Howard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Sunday Times Rich List (2020)
forbes_bio: Alan Howard cofounded Brevan Howard Asset Management, a European hedge fund specializing in macro trading, in 2002.
The firm was once one of the world's top macro hedge funds, with assets under management peaking at $40 billion in 2013.
A streak of uninspiring returns led to billions in investor withdrawals, but assets have rebounded to $36 billion after solid returns in recent years.
In 2019, Howard stepped down as CEO to focus solely on investing and to give portfolio managers more autonomy.

name: Xu Bo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2017-2019); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2015-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2023-2026)
forbes_bio: Xu Bo is the founder and chairman of Guangzhou Duoyi Network, one of China's largest mobile game companies.
Xu started the predecessor to Duoyi in 2006 with an investment from Kingsoft.

name: Wu Guanjiang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Wu Guanjiang is cofounder of Chongqing Zhifei Biological Products, a vaccine maker.
Wu, who was previously chairman, gradually reduced his stake and no longer has a management role in the company.
Zhifei listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.
Wu's fortune is comprised primarily from the sale of his shares over the years; his stake in Zhifei in now less than 5%.

name: Jim Thompson
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2016)
forbes_bio: Jim Thompson started his moving company, Crown Worldwide Group, in Japan in 1965, with $1,000.

Crown Worldwide is now one of the world's largest privately held relocation companies, with operations in 45 countries and more than 3,000 employees. It is also involved in document storage and fine-arts transportation.
Thompson moved the company's headquarters to Hong Kong in 1978. He is a permanent resident of Hong Kong.
A citizen of Ireland, he is a native of the state of New Jersey and owns a country estate in Ireland, near the home of his ancestors.
He resigned as chairman in 2025 and is now chairman emeritus; his daughter, Jennifer Harvey, is the group's CEO.
forbes_facts: In his adopted home, Hong Kong, Thompson served as chairman of the American Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong.
Thompson celebrates his birthday with an annual tradition of doing a push-up for every year of his life.

name: Zhao Lixin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2020)
forbes_bio: Zhao Lixin is the CEO of semiconductor supplier GalaxyCore.
GalaxyCore went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.
GalaxyCore's customers include Oppo, Xiaomi, Samsung and Lenovo.
GalaxyCore was founded in 2003.

name: Lam Kong
forbes_bio: Lam Kong chairs Hong Kong-listed China Medical System, which distributes drugs to thousands of hospitals around the country.
Lam founded the company in 1995, almost a decade after graduating from Zhanjiang Medical College.
China Medical went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2010.
China Medical System is the largest shareholder of Shanghai-listed Tibet Rhodiola Pharmaceutical.
China Medical System is headquartered in Shenzhen.

name: Diana Teh Li Shing
forbes_bio: Diana Teh Li Shing is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Her father founded the bank in 1966. Teh died in December 2022 at age 92.
Her father had a substantial minority stake in both Public Bank and insurance firm LPI Capital.
